Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨1t,t,2ln⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞)?

a
11+t⟨1,t2,2t⟩
b
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
c
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
d
11+t⟨−1,t2,22t⟩
e
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate: r'(t)=⟨-1/t²,1,√2/t⟩. Since t>0, its magnitude is √(1/t⁴+1+2/t²)=(1+t²)/t². Thus the unit tangent vector r'(t)/‖r'(t)‖ is ⟨-1,t²,√2t⟩/(1+t²), which is option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t},\,t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty )?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\sqrt{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+(1)^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}+1+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{1+{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-1,\,{t}^{2},\,\sqrt{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨1t,t,2ln⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞)?

a
11+t⟨1,t2,2t⟩
b
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
c
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
d
11+t⟨−1,t2,22t⟩
e
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t2⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(1t),ddt(t),2ddt(ln⁡t)⟩=⟨−1t2,1,2t⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t): ‖r′(t)‖=(−1t2)2+(1)2+(2t)2=1t4+1+2t2=1+t4+2t2t4=(1+t2)2t4=1+t2t2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve: T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=t21+t2⟨−1t2,1,2t⟩=11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩

content.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t},\,t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty )?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\sqrt{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+(1)^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}+1+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{1+{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-1,\,{t}^{2},\,\sqrt{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t+1,\,8\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2}+3⟩$ at the point $P(2,0,5)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,0,5)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2,0,5⟩ \\ ⟨t+1,\,8\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2}+3⟩ & =⟨2,0,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t+1=2 \\ 8\operatorname{ln}⁡t=0 \\ 2{t}^{2}+3=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,0,5)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\frac{8}{t},\,4t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨1,\,\frac{8}{1},\,4(1)⟩=⟨1,8,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+64+16} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,0,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨1,8,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{9},\frac{8}{9},\frac{4}{9}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,0,5)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2,0,5⟩ \\ ⟨t+1,\,8\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2}+3⟩ & =⟨2,0,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t+1=2 \\ 8\operatorname{ln}⁡t=0 \\ 2{t}^{2}+3=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,0,5)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\frac{8}{t},\,4t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨1,\,\frac{8}{1},\,4(1)⟩=⟨1,8,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+64+16} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,0,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨1,8,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{9},\frac{8}{9},\frac{4}{9}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨8t,\,3{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{3}⟩$ at the point $P(16,12,16)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(16,12,16)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨16,12,16⟩ \\ ⟨8t,\,3{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{3}⟩ & =⟨16,12,16⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}8t=16 \\ 3{t}^{2}=12 \\ 2{t}^{3}=16.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(16,12,16)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,6t,\,6{t}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =⟨8,\,6(2),\,6(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8,12,24⟩ \\  & =4⟨2,3,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =4\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{4+9+36} \\  & =4\sqrt{49} \\  & =28\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(16,12,16):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{28}\cdot 4⟨2,3,6⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{7},\frac{3}{7},\frac{6}{7}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨8t,\,3{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{3}⟩$ at the point $P(16,12,16)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(16,12,16)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨16,12,16⟩ \\ ⟨8t,\,3{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{3}⟩ & =⟨16,12,16⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}8t=16 \\ 3{t}^{2}=12 \\ 2{t}^{3}=16.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(16,12,16)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,6t,\,6{t}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =⟨8,\,6(2),\,6(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8,12,24⟩ \\  & =4⟨2,3,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =4\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{4+9+36} \\  & =4\sqrt{49} \\  & =28\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(16,12,16):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{28}\cdot 4⟨2,3,6⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{7},\frac{3}{7},\frac{6}{7}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By the product rule, r′(t)=−2sin(2t)p(t)+cos(2t)p′(t). At t=−π/6, this gives r′=√3(√3i+√3k)+(1/2)(−2i−8j+4k)=2i−4j+5k. Its magnitude is √45=3√5. Normalizing gives (2√5/15)i−(4√5/15)j+(√5/3)k, option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$, given that  $p(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k$ and $\,{p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})=-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})p(-\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3}){p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k) \\  & =(3\,i+3\,k)+(-\,i-4\,j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i-4\,j+5\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot (2\,i-4\,j+5\,k) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ is
 $T(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k.$

content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$, given that  $p(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k$ and $\,{p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})=-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k.$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})p(-\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3}){p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k) \\  & =(3\,i+3\,k)+(-\,i-4\,j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i-4\,j+5\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot (2\,i-4\,j+5\,k) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ is
 $T(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k.$

decision.explanation: The product rule gives r′(t)=−2t p(t)/(t²+1)²+p′(t)/(t²+1). At t=0, r′(0)=p′(0)=i−2j−2k, whose magnitude is √(1+4+4)=3. Dividing by 3 gives option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=0$, given that  $p(0)=2\,i+j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(0)=i-2\,j-2\,k.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2(0)}{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(0)+\frac{1}{{0}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =0(2\,i+j-k)+(\,i-2\,j-2k) \\  & =\,i-2\,j-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (i-2\,j-2\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is  $T(0)=\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k.$

content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2(0)}{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(0)+\frac{1}{{0}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =0(2\,i+j-k)+(\,i-2\,j-2k) \\  & =\,i-2\,j-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (i-2\,j-2\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is  $T(0)=\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k.$
